Rashi on Nazir 44a:12:1.hebrew: ומה טומאה שלא עשה מטמא כמיטמא - שהמטמא את הנזיר אינו עובר עליו, וכדמוכח בסמוך:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:12:1.english: And if [in the case of] impurity, in which [the Torah] did not make the one who renders impure like the one who becomes impure - For one who renders the nazirite impure does not violate [a prohibition] on his account, and as is demonstrated shortly:

Rashi on Nazir 44a:12:2.hebrew: תגלחת שעשה בה מגלח כמתגלח - שהמגלח את הנזיר עובר בלאו, כדלקמן: ״תער לא יעבור על ראשו״ — קרי ביה: לא יעביר ליה אחר:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:12:2.english: Shaving, in which [the Torah] made the one who shaves like the one who is shaved - For one who shaves a nazirite violates a negative commandment, as [stated] below: “No razor shall come upon his head” — read into it: Another [person] shall not pass [a razor] over him.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:15:1.english: The verse states: “And he renders impure his consecrated head” — to one who renders impure his consecrated head - Since it is not written: “And his consecrated head was rendered impure for him.”

Rashi on Nazir 44a:18:1.hebrew: אמר רחמנא ראשו וזקנו - דמייתרי, כדאמרינן לעיל, להתיר למצורע נזיר לגלח:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:18:1.english: The Merciful One states: “His head” and “his beard” - For they are superfluous, as we said above, to permit a leper [who is a] nazirite to shave.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:19:1.hebrew: בעינן גידול שיער - כדי לקיים בו מצות גילוח ביום הבאת קרבנותיו, וליכא:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:19:1.english: We require hair growth - In order to fulfill with it the mitzvah of shaving on the day of bringing his offerings, and there is none.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:1:1.hebrew: יכול - באחותו שהוא מותר, אבל לא בשל אחרים — לא בשדרה ולא בגולגולת על שאר קרובים:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:1:1.english: One might [have thought] - [That it is only] in [the case of] his sister that he is permitted, but not with [the remains] of others — neither for a spine nor for a skull for other relatives.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:1:2.hebrew: שגופה תלוי בה - בשדרה וגולגולת, שבכך עיקר הגוף תלוי — או בזה או בזה. ״אף כל״ — בשאר קרובים יכול ליטמא: או בשדרה, או בגולגולת, או ברוב בניינו, או ברוב מניינו, ואע"פ שהוא חסר משאר הגוף. וש"מ דמותר ליטמא לאביו אע"פ שהוא חסר — ותיקשה דרב חסדא: דהאיכא ר"א בן יעקב דקאמר נמי הכי, ושמע מינה דלכולי עלמא לית להו דרב חסדא, דאמר ״בזמן שהוא שלם ולא בזמן שהוא חסר״:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:1:2.english: That her body is dependent upon it - Upon the spine and skull, for upon this the body's essence depends — either upon this one or upon that one. “So too, every [person]” — regarding other relatives, he may become impure: either for a spine, or for a skull, or for most of his skeleton, or for most of his count [of bones], even though he is missing the rest of the body. And deduce from this that [a priest] is permitted to become impure for his father even though he is missing [parts] — and let [this] pose a difficulty to Rav Ḥisda: For here is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov who also says this! And deduce from it that everyone disagrees with [the opinion of] Rav Ḥisda, who said: “[Only] when he is whole, but not when he is missing”!

Rashi on Nazir 44a:20:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא - דתגלחת דסותר אלא משום דבעינן דתיהוי ליה גידול שיער? ואילו הכא, גבי יין, למה ליה למיסתר? הא קאי שערו דחזי לגילוח:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:20:1.english: Is the reason - that shaving negates [thirty days] anything other than because we require that he have hair growth? Whereas here, regarding wine, why should it negate? Behold, his hair remains, which is fit for shaving.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:2:1.hebrew: הא נמי ר"י היא - כלומר, הוא דאמר כר"י, ורב [חסדא] דאמר — כי האי תנא:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:2:1.english: That too is Rabbi Yehuda - That is to say, he is the one who stated [his opinion] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and Rav [Ḥisda], who stated [his view], stated [it] in accordance with this tanna.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:2:2.hebrew: דתניא מעשה שמת אביו של רבי יצחק הכהן בגינזק ובאו והודיעוהו לאחר שלש שנים ובא ושאל את רבי יהושע בן אלישע וד' זקנים שעמו - מהו ליטמא ולהביאו בקברי אבותיו:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:2:2.english: As it is taught: An incident occurred in which the father of Rabbi Yitzḥak the priest died in Ginzak, and they came and informed him after three years, and he came and asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Elisha and four Elders who were with him - [He asked them:] What is [the law regarding whether he may] become impure and bring him to the graves of his ancestors?

Rashi on Nazir 44a:3:1.hebrew: ואמרו לו לאביו בזמן שהוא שלם ולא בזמן שהוא חסר - ולאחר שלש שנים, אי אפשר לו שאינו חסר:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:3:1.english: And they said to him: “For his father” — when he is whole, and not when he is lacking - And after three years, it is impossible for [the body] not to be lacking.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:5:1.english: And impurity and shaving were permitted - Through the shaving of a leper [metzora] and through a corpse with no one to bury it [met mitzva].

Rashi on Nazir 44a:6:1.english: As impurity negates all - Even in [the case of] a lengthy naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:6:2.hebrew: וחייבין עליה קרבן - אשם, ותורין או בני יונה:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:6:2.english: And he is liable to [bring] an offering for it - A guilt-offering, and turtledoves or young pigeons:

Rashi on Nazir 44a:6:3.english: And shaving negates only thirty days - And [this applies] even in a long naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ל לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא - מכדי כתיב: "על כל נפשות מת", "לאביו" למה לי? אלא, להכי הוא דאתא: דלאביו לא יטמא, אבל מיטמא הוא למת מצוה:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:8:1.english: The verse states: “For his father or for his mother he shall not become impure” - Now, since it is written: “[He shall not come near] any dead body,” why do I need “for his father”? Rather, it comes for this: that for his father he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a met mitzva.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:9:1.hebrew: ויין יותר מכללו - כגון גבי יין מצוה שנשבע עליו לשתותו, מק"ו: ומה טומאה כו':
Rashi on Nazir 44a:9:1.english: And let wine be exempted from its general prohibition - For instance, regarding wine of a mitzvah that he took an oath to drink, from an a fortiori argument: Just as impurity, etc.

Rashi on Nazir 44a:9:2.hebrew: לאסור יין מצוה - שנשבע עליו, כיין רשות, וכדר"ש בפ"ק דמסכתין (דף ג:). והאי דמותר בקידושא ואבדלתא, דלא חשיב ליה הותר מכללו — משום דלא חל עליו מעולם נזירות, משום דנשבע ועומד מהר סיני הוא; ומותר מכללו לא קחשיב ליה, אלא היכא דחייל, ואח"כ מישתרי בהו:
Rashi on Nazir 44a:9:2.english: To prohibit wine of a mitzva - [Such as wine] about which he took an oath [to drink it, to prohibit it] like optional wine; and [this is] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon in the first chapter of our tractate (page 3b). And this [fact] that he is permitted [wine] for *kiddush* and *havdala*, which [the Gemara] does not consider “permitted from its general prohibition” — [this is] because naziriteship never took effect upon it, because he is [already] under oath from Mount Sinai; and [the Gemara] considers [a prohibition] “permitted from its general prohibition” only where it took effect and was afterward permitted with regard to them.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:11:1.english: "For [his naziriteship] was rendered impure" - (negating from the beginning: for his naziriteship was rendered impure) "His naziriteship" is an exclusion.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:12:1.english: "That [the Torah] did not make the one who renders impure like the one who becomes impure" - One who renders the nazirite impure does not incur lashes.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:12:2.hebrew: שעשו בה המגלח - את הנזיר; כמתגלח — כנזיר עצמו, וילקו שניהן, כדדרשינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:12:2.english: "In which they made the one who shaves" - [I.e., one who shaves] the nazirite; "like the one who is shaved" — like the nazirite himself, and both of them receive lashes, as we expound nearby.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:15:1.hebrew: אמר קרא ראשו - גבי מצורע, להתיר מצורע נזיר:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:15:1.english: "The verse states: 'His head'" - [This is stated] with regard to a leper, to permit a nazirite leper [to shave].

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:19:1.hebrew: תגלחת שהותרה מכללה אינו דין שלא תסתור - וא"ת: טומאה תוכיח? וי"ל: מה לטומאה — שכן סותרת את הכל:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:19:1.english: "Shaving, which is exempted from its general prohibition, is it not logical that it should not negate" - And if you say: Let [ritual] impurity prove [otherwise]? One can answer: What [comparison is there] to [ritual] impurity, as it negates everything.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:20:1.hebrew: ומה תגלחת שהותרה מכללה סותרת - וא"ת: מה לתגלחת שכן עשה בה מגלח כמתגלח, תאמר [ביין] שלא עשה משקה כשותה? וי"ל: דמהאי טעמא נעשה בו משקה [כשותה]; אבל בתר דמשני דיין [אינו סותר] — דין הוא דלא נעשה בו משקה כשותה, הואיל דלא סותר:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:20:1.english: "And if shaving, which is exempted from its general prohibition, negates [thirty days]" - And if you say: What [comparison is there] to shaving, in that [the Torah] made the one who shaves [another] like the one who is shaved; can you say [the same] of [wine], where it did not make the one who gives drink like the one who drinks? And one can say: For this [very] reason, let us make regarding it the one who gives drink like [the one who drinks]! But after [the Gemara] answers that wine [does not negate], it is logical that we do not make regarding it the one who gives drink like the one who drinks, since it does not negate.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:2:1.hebrew: ובאו והודיעוהו לאחר ג' שנים ושאל את ר' יהושע בן [אלישע] - זקנו, שהיה רוצה לקברו בקברי אבותיו, ואמר לו: "לאביו" — בזמן שהוא שלם:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:2:1.english: "And they came and informed him after three years, and he asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben [Elisha]" - [Rabbi Yehoshua was] his grandfather; for [Rabbi Yitzḥak] wanted to bury him in his ancestral burial ground, and [Rabbi Yehoshua] said to him: [The verse states] "for his father" [only] when he is whole.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:4:1.hebrew: חומר בטומאה ובתגלחת שסותרין - טומאה — בהדיא כתיב: "והימים הראשונים יפלו". ותגלחת שסותרת שלשים, כדאמרינן לקמן — משום דבעינן גידול שיער כדי גידול שיער סתם נזירות, שיהא השער בשעת תגלחת מצוה:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:4:1.english: "A stricture with regard to impurity and shaving, that they negate" - [With regard to] impurity, it is explicitly written: "And the previous days shall fall away" (Numbers 6:12). And [as for] shaving, which negates thirty [days], as we say later — [this is] because we require hair growth equivalent to the hair growth of an unspecified naziriteship, so that there will be hair at the time of the mitzvah shaving.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:4:2.hebrew: והיוצא מן הגפן אינו סותר - בהדיא ממעטינן ליה בגמ':
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:4:2.english: "And that which emerges from the vine does not negate" - We explicitly exclude it in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:5:1.hebrew: חומר ביוצא מן הגפן שלא הותר מכללו - לאסור יין מצוה כיין הרשות: שאם נשבע "שאשתה", ואח"כ נדר בנזיר — אסור [ביין]. ותגלחת הותרה בתגלחת מצורע, [כדאמרינן לקמן] (דף נח.) "מראשו"; וטומאה הותרה במת מצוה:
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:5:1.english: A stricture with regard to that which emerges from the vine, that it was not exempted from its general prohibition - [This serves] to forbid wine of a mitzvah like optional wine: for if he swore, "I shall drink," and afterward vowed [to become] a nazirite, he is forbidden [from wine]. And shaving was permitted in [the case of] the shaving of a leper [metzora], [as we say below] (58a) from [the verse's words] "his head"; and [contracting] ritual impurity was permitted in [the case of] a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse].

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:9:1.english: "And let wine be exempted from its general prohibition" - [This refers] to one who swore: "I will drink [wine]."

Tosafot on Nazir 44a:9:2.hebrew: אמר קרא מיין ושכר - דמיותר, כדאמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל נזיר דף ג:):
Tosafot on Nazir 44a:9:2.english: "The verse states: 'From wine and strong drink'" - For [this phrase] is superfluous, as we say in the first chapter (above, Nazir 3b).
